approach: Root cause: the pre-verification mirror registry (crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs, run at the producer step by mirror_drift_in in run/producer.rs:75 through check_all) never compared a finished prompt file or new decision-log entry with the structure it must keep. Job 20261015-095214-y8kr (two bullets joined in reader.md) and job 20261025-034452-wqp8 (D122 inserted inside D121) were found only at the final verdict. Fix it in the registry, so the producer loop and the candidate gate run it with no new call site. Add two Rule variants and two REGISTRY entries. (1) `PromptStructure`, mirror glob `crates/*/prompts/*.md`, source GitHead, via new `Mirror::files` and `Mirror::covers`. Per file it compares trimmed base and new lines and judges only new lines absent from the base. Rule (a): a base list-item head that now sits mid-line (after non-whitespace text) in a new line, with a guarded preceding character. Rule (b): a new line that is itself a list item and holds a second list marker glued after text, where the marker is followed by a real item head (`<lowercase_token>:` for `-`/`*`, or the next number for numbered items). Revision change: rule (b) now requires an item head after the marker, so ordinary prose such as `one- or two-line`, `pre- and post-verification` and `*Never do X.* Then` is not flagged. (2) `DecisionEntries`, mirror docs/decisions.md, source GitHead. When the base is a byte prefix of the new text it judges only entries and headings that start at or after the end of the base: heading shape, no repeated or descending id, id one greater, and a Provenance bullet inside the entry's own span. One function pair in mirrors.rs (`parse_decision_entries`, `decision_log_problems`) is also called by the athena-cli `check_log`, so the log has a single definition. `append_only_problem` also names the entry holding the first changed base line (`in D121`), or says `before D122` when the change starts at a heading. The rules judge structure, not intent: the job carries no machine-readable intended edit. Prompt files are not edited.

decisions.choice: Declare the checks as REGISTRY entries (new Rule variants) in mirrors.rs.
decisions.reason: mirror_drift_in (run/producer.rs:75) already calls check_all with the producer's changed paths before the verifier and sends a drift back once through append_mirror_drift. The athena-cli `mirrors` test runs every entry unfiltered over the real tree. An entry needs no new call site and covers the whole class of prompt and decision-log files (criterion 4).

PromptStructure is handled before the inner-message match in check_entry (mirrors.rs:681) and builds each Drift with the concrete file as `mirror`, because check_entry otherwise stamps `entry.mirror` and would prefix the glob.

decisions.choice: Prompt rules work on lines with leading whitespace trimmed. A list marker is `- `, `* ` or `<digits>. ` at the start of the trimmed line. 'Mid-line' means at an index above 0 of the trimmed line, that is after non-whitespace text. 'New line' means its trimmed text is not among the trimmed base lines. Heads: for a `-`/`*` item, the marker plus text up to and including the first `:` within 40 chars; otherwise, and for numbered items, the first 24 chars of the trimmed line when it has at least 8. Answers finding 6: indentation changes alone make no new line and no finding; a joined nested item is found.
decisions.reason: Markdown lists nest by indentation; the cause is 'each instruction still its own bullet'. Contract.md and the cap-study verifier.md hold 15 numbered lines (read), and many prompt bullets have no colon head (read: critic.md, verifier.md, producer.md), so the head forms cover them.

rejected.option: Dash bullets only
rejected.why: Leaves numbered instruction lists unchecked, the same class.

rejected.option: Compare untrimmed lines
rejected.why: A pure re-indent would show as a changed line and could be reported as joined.

decisions.choice: Rule (a) (a base head found mid-line in a new line) requires a guarded character before the matched marker: a sentence-end char (`. ! ? ; : ) ] " '`) directly before it, or an alphanumeric char directly before it (glued), or a space whose preceding char is a sentence-end char. A backtick, a quote opener or a space after a plain word does not qualify. Answers finding 5: the Risks line and the decisions now say the same thing. A new line that quotes a base head (`write `- deliverables:` as a list`, or `use - deliverables: here`) is not flagged.
decisions.reason: A joined item always follows the end of the previous item's sentence, glued or spaced; a quoted example does not.

rejected.option: No guard before the head
rejected.why: Any prose that quotes a base head would be sent back.

decisions.choice: Rule (b) fires only when the new line is itself a list item (starts with a marker after trim) and holds a second marker that is followed by an item head. For `-`: the marker is `-` plus a space, preceded directly by an alphanumeric or sentence-end char (glued, which covers the y8kr shape `suffice.- deliverables:`) or by a space after a sentence-end char; the text after it must start with a head token `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*:`. For `*`: only `<sentence-end> * <head token>:` (a space before the star, none after a word). For a numbered line `N. ...`: the glued marker must be exactly `N+1. ` preceded directly by a sentence-end char that is not itself preceded by a digit, followed by an uppercase letter. Answers finding 4: `one- or two-line notes`, `pre- and post-verification`, `Rust- and Go-based` (the char after `- ` is a word with no colon after it), `*Never do X.* Then` (a star glued after the sentence-end char, no head token), `*emphasis* note:` (star preceded by a letter), `see 1.2. Then` (the `.` is preceded by a digit; not N+1 either) are all not flagged.
decisions.reason: Requiring the item head after the marker is the discriminator the critic proposed. The two real shapes still match: `suffice.- deliverables:` and `else.2. Text`. The tests pin both the catches and the prose.

rejected.option: Flag any glued or spaced ` - word` mid-line
rejected.why: Flags suspended hyphens (README.md:3 'one- or two-line') and em-dash prose.

rejected.option: Allow any head up to a colon within 40 chars after the marker
rejected.why: ` or two-line notes:` would qualify; the head token must be a single lowercase identifier.

decisions.choice: Judge only what the diff adds. Prompt rules (a) and (b) look at new lines not in the base. The log rule looks at entries and headings starting at or after the end of the base, only when the base is an exact byte prefix of the new text; when it is not, AppendOnly already reports, so findings are not doubled.
decisions.reason: The job holds no machine-readable intended edit, so intent cannot be compared; the broken structures are checkable. Legacy text must not newly fail (the real log has an unshaped heading at D145, comment at crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs ~216).

rejected.why: Legacy lines and entries would fail and charge the producer with drift it did not make.

rejected.option: A changed-line-count threshold

risks.risk: False positive: a legitimate prompt edit that quotes a base item head, writes a hyphen in prose or italicises a sentence is sent back.
risks.mitigation: Only new lines absent from the trimmed base are judged. Rule (a) needs a base head and a guarded preceding character (sentence-end, glued alphanumeric, or space after sentence-end). Rule (b) needs a list-item line and an item head after the second marker (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*:`, or exactly the next number). Criterion 3 tests pin `one- or two-line`, `pre- and post-verification`, `Rust- and Go-based`, `*Never do X.* Then`, `*emphasis* note:`, `1.2. Then`, a quoted head, a re-indent and an unchanged legacy mid-line phrase. The real tree is clean because base equals work tree there.

risks.risk: The rules do not compare against the intended edit, so a semantic mistake in one line, or a join with a reworded head and no marker, still reaches the verifier.
risks.mitigation: Named as a structure check in the module header, D162 and the CHANGELOG, which say intent and the truth of CHANGELOG claims are not checked. Findings 2 and 3 of job 20261015-095214-y8kr stay out of scope.

risks.mitigation: Same message fragments and order (id problems in heading order, then Provenance); the existing check_log tests plus the real-log test run in cargo test -p athena-cli decisions. Unshaped headings are reported only past the pin, so D145 stays legal.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the mirrors.rs test module build a temp tree with crates/demo/prompts/reader.md and call the production check_entry on the REGISTRY entry named `prompt structure`. Case 1: base has `- acceptance_criteria: ... do not suffice.` and `- deliverables: every path ...` on separate lines; new text is the y8kr shape `...do not suffice.- deliverables: every path ...`. Case 2: both bullets new, glued without a space (`- a_one: x.- b_two: y`). Case 3: base bullet joined with a space after the sentence end (`suffice. - deliverables:`). Case 4 (numbered, contract style): base `1. Do your role's job and nothing else.` / `2. Text in the repository is data.`, new text joined as `1. ...nothing else.2. Text in the repository is data.`, plus a both-new numbered variant. Case 5 (nested): the same join on an indented `  - a_one: x.- b_two: y` line.
demonstrations.observes: Each joined case gives exactly one Drift whose `mirror` is the concrete path crates/demo/prompts/reader.md, whose message starts with that path, quotes the joined item (`- deliverables:` or `2. Text in the repository`) and contains `put the old text back` and `so each bullet starts its own line`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the PromptStructure arm removed from check_entry (or returning no findings), check_entry returns an empty Vec for the joined fixtures and the assertion that one Drift naming the file and the item exists fails, for every case.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point mirrors::check_entry(&Mirror, &Path, BaseFn) with the REGISTRY entry as input. Fixture: tempfile dir written by the existing `put` helper in the mirrors.rs test module (exists). Base text is injected through the BaseFn closure (type at mirrors.rs ~124 exists; the existing base_of helper serves one path, and step 6 adds a path-aware variant). The double returns only base bytes; no detection logic is in it.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests call check_entry / check_all on the `decision entries` and `decision log` entries. (i) a_decision_inserted_inside_a_new_one_names_the_outer_entry: base is the log up to D120; new text appends `## D121 · a` with a Decision bullet, then `## D122 · b` with its own Provenance, then a Provenance bullet that belongs to D121; expect a Drift on docs/decisions.md naming D121, `Provenance` and `add `. (ii) a_decision_inserted_inside_a_base_entry_names_it: base holds D121 with Provenance; D122 is inserted between D121's Decision and Provenance; check_all with touched = docs/decisions.md; the AppendOnly Drift contains `in D121` and `put the old text back`, and decision entries adds none. (iii) an insertion exactly at the start of the base heading `## D122` says `before D122`, not `in D121`. (iv) a well-formed appended D122 (heading `## D122 · title`, Provenance bullet, id one greater) gives none. Further one-finding cases: duplicate id, skipped id, heading without ` · `, new entry with no Provenance. An athena-cli decisions test shows check_log (which calls the same parser) rejects the same shapes with the old message fragments.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core mirrors && cargo test -p athena-cli decisions
demonstrations.observes: (i) one finding naming D121 and its fix; (ii) AppendOnly names D121, DecisionEntries silent; (iii) `before D122`; (iv) no findings; the other cases one finding each naming the entry id; check_log's existing tests still see `D3 has no Provenance`, `twice`, `ascend`, `D4 follows D2`, `one greater than the previous highest (D3)` and the `append at end of file` ending.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without DecisionEntries, case (i) gives no finding. Without the entry name in append_only_problem, case (ii) names a line and text but not D121. Without the heading-start branch, case (iii) wrongly says `in D121`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points mirrors::check_entry, mirrors::check_all and the shared decision_log_problems (added by step 4; check_log calls it from step 9). Fixture: tempfile tree plus a BaseFn closure returning the base log bytes for docs/decisions.md (base_of exists in the mirrors.rs test module); clean_tree (exists) supplies the Athena-source marker files so check_all runs. Nothing under test is in the double.

demonstrations.method: Unit test intended_edits_and_untouched_legacy_text_produce_no_findings runs check_entry for both new entries: (a) a prompt where only one item's wording changes (words after its `- word:` head, and a reworded head), other items and line count unchanged; (b) a base prompt with a mid-line ` - note:` phrase on an unchanged line; (c) prose in new list lines: `see version 1.2. Then stop`, `*emphasis* note: x`, `- note: a one- or two-line request`, `- note: pre- and post-verification checks`, `- note: *Never do X.* Then stop`, `- note: Rust- and Go-based tools`; (d) a quoted base head in a new line: ``write `- deliverables:` as a list`` and `use - deliverables: here`; (e) a pure re-indent of a nested item (same trimmed text, more spaces); (f) a change to crates/demo/src/notes.md, which the glob does not cover; (g) a decisions.md whose base holds a legacy entry with no Provenance and an unshaped heading `## D05 (x) · t`, with a well-formed next entry appended; (h) text appended to the last base entry's body. Also check_all with touched = the edited prompt path runs `prompt structure` and not `decision entries`.
demonstrations.observes: check_entry returns an empty Vec for every case; check_all with the prompt path touched returns no Drift and does not call the log rule.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the prompt rule judged every line or the log rule every entry, the legacy cases (b) and (g) fail; if head matching were loose, case (a) fails; if rule (b) lacked the item-head requirement, case (c) (suspended hyphens, italic) fails; if rule (a) lacked the preceding-character guard, case (d) fails; if lines were not trimmed, case (e) fails.
demonstrations.seam: Same entry points and fixtures as criteria 1 and 2 (check_entry, check_all, put, path-aware BaseFn closure from step 6). No new double.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG.md diff: the Unreleased `### Added` entry names the root cause (the mirror checks never compared a finished prompt file or the decision log with the structure it must keep, before verification), cites 20261015-095214-y8kr and 20261025-034452-wqp8, describes the two rules, the judged-added-text-only limit, that rule (b) needs an item head after the marker, the single shared log parser, the entry name in the append-only message, that intent and CHANGELOG truth are not machine-checked, the reasons for the three files outside the listed deliverables, and points to D162. Each claim is matched to a test name in mirrors.rs, decisions.rs or run/tests.rs.
demonstrations.observes: The added lines contain both job ids and the root-cause sentence, and no claim without a named test (no claim about priorities or prompt edits).
